verifier_note: Checked all 27 unique warrant sources by retrieval (Rust Reference, Cargo Book, rustc Book, rustup Book, and 5 blog/release-notes posts, all 2021+) and independently reproduced nearly every measured 'how' claim myself with rustc/cargo/rustup 1.98.1 in scratch directories (never inside si-rpg-engine): the caret-range and --locked error messages (recipe 3), the rust-version rejection and all three 'Locking to latest Rust X.Y' message variants (recipe 8), the cwd-vs-manifest-path toolchain/config split (recipe 9), Cargo's actual release-profile rustc flags and the workspace-member profile warning (recipe 5), the virtual-workspace resolver-default warning and the workspace.lints-to---forbid mapping (recipe 6), the 4-package feature-union cfg lists and cargo tree -i output (recipe 4), cargo fix --edition's exact 3-fix diff (recipe 7), the four-mutually-exclusive-RUSTFLAGS-sources matrix (recipe 10), and the wasm pub-export gotcha (recipe 1). For recipe 2 I rebuilt the actual solver crate (fetched read-only from mcp-tool-shop-org/si-rpg-engine via gh api) in a scratch copy with rapier3d-f64 0.35.3 and reproduced the crate-type-changes-the-digest claim almost exactly: my absolute byte counts differed from the recipe's (different Cargo.lock resolution / no --remap-path-prefix) but the delta from adding rlib was +28 bytes in both, and the dependency-graph shape (45 lib, 4 proc-macro, 8 build-script bin, 1 cdylib) matched exactly. Every engine_note fact checked against the live repo (Cargo.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, .cargo/config.toml, Cargo.lock package count/versions, lib.rs/rapier_law.rs source, build.mjs) matched verbatim. I found zero currency or attribution defects. The one systemic weakness is mechanical, not a knowledge gap: two checks (recipe 2's check 1 and recipe 6's check 3) have a label that bundles two claims ('exports X and imports nothing', 'compiles and without a warning') but the check body only encodes an oracle assertion for the first half (missing wasm_no_imports:true / no_warnings:true respectively), so the oracle would silently keep passing if the unasserted half regressed. I verified both unasserted halves are true today by building the exact check sources directly, so this is a check-authoring completeness gap, not a wrong claim.
